answer.location_description: Whole image: a horizontal grating of 2-row bands with a period of 4 rows (rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 bright; rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 dark). It spans the full width and height, not just the nodule.
answer.shortcut_type: periodic horizontal stripe / scan-line grating artifact
answer.mechanism: Layer-1 units 8, 9, 10, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 29 are matched filters for the stripe in phase A. Their row-pair weights alternate sign, so a uniform image largely cancels, and their large negative biases (about -61 to -97) mean they fire only when the stripes are present. These units feed strongly positive into layer-2 units u3, u4, u10, u12 and u13, whose output weights are +63, +77, +67, +42 and +71. They also feed negatively into u1 and u7, whose output weights are -94 and -99. Units 2, 3, 23 and 31 hold the opposite phase with large positive biases (about +65 to +99), so they are normally on. They drive the benign-voting units u1 and u7 and inhibit u3, u4 and u13. A phase-A grating therefore turns off this benign drive while switching on the malignant pathway, pushing the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: Unit 8 rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 are mostly +20 to +60, while rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 are mostly -20 to -60. Units 9, 10, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 29 show the same pattern, as does unit 1 more weakly. Units 2, 3, 23 and 31 show the exact inverse (e.g. unit 31 row 2 is about +30 to +56 and row 4 is about -10 to -55). The stripes are uniform across all 24 columns and extend to the image corners, unlike any nodule-centred structure. Layer-2 weights: u4 receives +93 from unit 27, +83 from unit 24, +74 from unit 20 and +63 from units 9 and 10. u13 receives +99 from unit 9 and +75 from unit 27. u1 receives -89 from unit 20 and -73 from unit 9, against +54 from unit 23 and +44 from unit 31. Output weights are u4 +77, u13 +71, u3 +63, u1 -94 and u7 -99. Units 0, 4-7, 11-17, 19, 21, 22, 25, 26, 28 and 30 look like untrained noise with small weights.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the stripes, the same units carry localized deviations near and off the image centre: strongly negative weights around rows 8-11, cols 16-19, and phase-breaking positive weights around rows 14-15, cols 9-12. These likely respond to nodule density, shape and margin, with bright, irregular nodule tissue near the centre read as malignant.
